speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: asked the Minister for Manpower in the past six months (a) how many workers aged 50 years and above have become unemployed; (b) what is the average length of time for them to be employed again; and (c) whether such data can be reported by the Ministry to the public periodically.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Just a reminder to Members to just mention the question number.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As for the first set of questions for this next set, I will also address questions that are for the next Sitting or for Written Answers that are related.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The reason is that, this approach allows us to deal with them more holistically.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To Ms Ng's question, MOM publishes the Labour Market Report on a quarterly basis and the Report on Labour Force in Singapore on an annual basis.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it is 90,500 in June 2020, as compared to 73,900 in December 2019.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is a difference of 16,600 over six months.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Of those unemployed, one in three were aged 50 and over, and this proportion has been and continues to be stable.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In comparison, about one in four persons in our resident workforce is aged 50 and over.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is consistent with the longer time they have taken to return to the workforce if they exit.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Based on latest available data on the duration of unemployment, the median period for residents aged 50 and over was 12 weeks.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This duration has been broadly stable for a number of years.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But we should expect it to rise in times of economic downturn, as it is likely to for all age groups, although the extent really remains to be seen.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In our labour statistics compilation, being placed on unpaid leave is captured as “temporary layoffs”.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In the first half of 2020, an estimated 11,050 Singapore Citizens were affected by temporary layoffs, compared to 33,000 non-citizens.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Since the start of the circuit breaker on 6 April 2020, employers with more than 10 employees are required to notify MOM within one week of implementing cost-saving measures, such as shorter work hours or no-pay leave, that result in more than 25% reduction in gross monthly salary for local employees or 25% reduction in basic monthly salary for foreign employees.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Based on the notifications received between the start of the circuit breaker period and 20 August 2020, salary reductions of more than 50% are a small minority.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are not able to provide the breakdown between Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents as the distinction was not made in the notification by employers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Government continues to monitor the job market closely and adjust its measures to support workers and help businesses maintain or expand their local employment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The National Jobs Council is coordinating efforts to provide 100,000 jobs and skills opportunities for jobseekers under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui asked about the take-up of these programmes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: MOM has started providing weekly updates on the jobs and skills situation to highlight the opportunities available for jobseekers and how they can access them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have helped to place over 25,000 individuals into jobs, traineeships and training places.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Of these, 24,000 across various age groups were placed into new jobs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: About half are in the public sector, with another quarter in the Modern Services and Lifestyle sectors.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The salary range of jobs can vary, depending on the sector and the specific job roles that an individual takes up.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Over 1,000 fresh graduate trainees have taken up traineeships under the SGUnited Traineeships programme.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The majority of the traineeship positions filled are in growth sectors, such as Information Communications Technology and Media, Professional Services, and Financial Services.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As the process of shortlisting and selecting suitable trainees by host organisations takes time, we can expect to see more placements into traineeships and company attachments subsequently.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Lastly, close to 700 trainees have enrolled in 40 courses under the SGUnited Skills Programme.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have expanded outreach to increase awareness of these opportunities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To reach out to fresh graduates on opportunities under the SGUnited Traineeships programme, WSG works closely with MOE, the Institutes of Higher Learning, NTUC and the People’s Association.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To reach out to mid-career individuals on attachments under the SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programme, WSG organises SGUnited Jobs and Skills Fairs to allow them to apply for opportunities onsite.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Twenty-four SGUnited Jobs & Skills Centres have also been set up across all HDB towns.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We also reach out to both groups through digital media channels.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: From January to July 2020, 36,400 jobseekers received basic career advisory or job search assistance through WSG and NTUC-e2i’s career matching services.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is 30% more than the same period in 2019, despite Circuit Breaker measures.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The traineeships and attachments do not automatically convert into a permanent job.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, we are hopeful that companies will find a good number of trainees to be a good fit and make them part of their permanent staff.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This will depend largely on the fit of each trainee to the job, and the business situation and hiring needs of the host organisation when the traineeships or attachments are completed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Workforce Singapore’s experience with the Attach-and-Train programmes so far has been that host organisations that are impressed with trainees will place them in full-time positions in the companies to make the most of the time and money that they have invested in the attachment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This will also help spur the hiring of trainees.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I should add that in designing the Jobs Growth Incentive, we made sure to double the support for more mature jobseekers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For cases where the traineeship does not result in a permanent job, the experience will equip the trainee with industry-relevant knowledge and skills, and help to burnish their credentials and value proposition to other employers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Government will also continue to support them in their job search journey, through career matching services offered by WSG and NTUC’s Employability and Employment Institute, and other partner organisations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms He Ting Ru asked about the safeguards against misuse.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Singapore Business Federation or SBF, our programme partner for these programmes, scrutinises each application to ensure that host companies structure their traineeships and attachments appropriately with clear development plans, so that participants can have a meaningful experience.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SBF also scrutinises the applications to make sure that the companies are not using these programmes to hire workers for permanent jobs at low cost.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Host organisations are required to declare in their applications if they had undertaken retrenchment exercises or adopted various cost-cutting measures.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some host organisations have asked if they can pay more than the stipulated allowances for very attractive candidates.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Instead of traineeships or attachments, they are advised to offer paid employment to these very attractive candidates, which will also enjoy significant support under the Jobs Growth Incentive.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In addition to the rigorous screening process that I have described above, SBF also assists companies to review and improve their proposals, especially for applications that are incomplete or lacking in detail.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These measures are necessary so that the traineeship or attachment experience is a positive and meaningful one.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is why it has taken four to six weeks, on average, to approve the applications, to ensure that the trainees’ interests are safeguarded.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SBF has stepped up resources in response to the strong interest in these programmes to process these applications as quickly as possible.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Would the Ministry consider publishing monthly, more granular updates available, especially during crisis periods like what we are going through at the moment?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: This is for us to be able to monitor and see whether the many, many schemes that have been introduced are working and how effective they are, whether there are areas that need extra support.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: The second is whether we will consider also publishing – because I notice the Minister answered the question about the number of Singaporeans who were retrenched, but that figure sometimes seems to also include residents – so, whether we can have a bit more granularity as well between Singaporeans and PRs?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Ultimately, Singaporeans do not have the back-up option of returning to their home countries.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, I think there is some value in knowing the data about whether Singaporeans are more affected.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Thirdly, have there been any public sector retrenchments so far this year?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: It is good that SBF has agreed to partner with MOM.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: However, I am just wondering whether we can have a bit more structure in this sort of on-going assessment reports of employers who have taken part in the schemes.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: For example, whether there will be monitoring visits being undertaken, whether we can publish regular achievement rates and information on how successful these companies are in converting traineeships into permanent job placements.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And, finally, whether the trainees themselves will be given a chance to provide feedback on the schemes and also on the specific employers.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: These, all together, will help everyone make sure that these schemes are not abused and are maximally effective.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This submission has to be signed off by the trainee himself or herself.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SBF has also made available their staff to handle incidents where the trainee feels that the programme is not well structured or they are not learning as much as they would like.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: SBF commits its resources to intervening in these cases.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, this aspect of the work that Ms He thinks is important, we agree.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As to whether they convert into placements subsequently, we are also interested to know and we will keep track of it as best as we can.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Because even if a person does not stay in employment with the host company, it does not necessarily mean that the traineeship was not useful.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Quite often, individuals, having completed the training, move on to other better options for employment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I think we will keep track of it, but we must know that we have to interpret that data quite carefully.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As to whether the public sector has retrenched, the public sector has actually leaned forward to bring hiring in advance of our needs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Quite a large number of the positions that are made available to jobseekers are because the public sector, having looked at their developmental plans and deciding that instead of hiring six months or nine months later, bring these forward so that the jobseekers can have a wider range of options and they can also have meaningful employment during this much more difficult time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To the question on the data, the data I described was exactly what you wanted – citizens.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I am not sure whether that got carried across clearly enough.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It was not a combination of citizens and PRs.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Member asked for citizens; we have provided the Member with the citizen data.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In fact, I also contrasted it to what was happening for the non-citizens, if the Member can go back and take a look at that.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Can we report employment statistics on a more regular basis?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That has also been the reason why Minister Chan Chun Sing and I, almost on a weekly basis now, have been visiting companies, different sectors to showcase the job, the opportunities available.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: During those occasions, we always publish a job situation report, different dimensions of it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it is not a question of whether we can provide the statistics more regularly.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: You may want to take off your mask.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I am very heartened to know that the MOM exercises compassion in the way they approach the various challenges in hiring practices that micro-enterprises and SMEs encounter to support them to adopt the correct and desired hiring practices.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: My supplementary question is related to the overarching issue of unfair hiring or workplace practices.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I understand that so far proactive surveillance has surfaced more of these companies than complaints by job seekers or employees.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: In my encounter with my residents, I do see that there is a lot of hesitance and uncertainty by employees or jobseekers when they encounter unfair hiring or workplace practices.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: They are not sure or not confident of raising these issues to the correct authorities.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: My question is, will the Minister consider increasing efforts in jobseeker or employee education efforts to reassure people and empower them that if they are aggrieved in any of their experiences while seeking jobs or within their workplace environment, they can safely blow the whistle.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: And what is the recourse that they have?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Because I think they have concerns and on repercussions on the employability in the future.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We have to approach the companies in a smart way, so as not to reveal their identity.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Our officers proactively reach out to these workers who we believe are in slightly more vulnerable positions – less likely to know their rights, less likely to know what the employers are supposed to do for them and meet statutory obligations.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I appreciate that Members, especially new Members are keen and enthusiastic.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I would just like to remind Members that for supplementary questions, they are subject to the same Standing Orders as ordinary questions.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And ordinary questions shall not contain more than one issue and shall be concise.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, I would urge the Members to be concise in their questioning.
